title: Ronnie Reads The Fine Print
description: Advice hour on Snazzie FM. Listeners bring real legal nightmares, jury summonses, liens, I R S letters, and Ronnie cures every one of them by simply not reading them. Barry has skimmed an actual statute. It does not help.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight we're solving your legal troubles. Subpoenas, summonses, liens, the whole alphabet. Bring me your paperwork, folks, and I'll tell you what it really says.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, I do want to say, I read a little of the statute before the show, and I'm not sure we're qualified to...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Reading is what gets people in trouble, Barry. First caller, Mildred, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, hello, dear. I got a jury duty summons, and it's the same day as my granddaughter's recital, and the letter says I could be arrested if I don't show up. I'm just terrified.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, first of all, congratulations. <p:0.3> You were selected. They don't send these to just anybody. Jury duty is invitation only. Honestly? I'd frame it.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: But, dear, the arrest part?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Here's the trick. Just don't sign the form. An unsigned summons is legally just a pamphlet. You can recycle a pamphlet, Mildred.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is... that is not how a summons works. You don't sign those, they're served.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Go to the recital, Mildred. Next up, Steve. What've you got?

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Yeah, so, I ignored one parking ticket, and now there's a lien on my car, and they're saying they're gonna take the whole vehicle. It's my only car, man.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Easy fix, Steve. Park it somewhere they legally can't tow it from. <p:0.3> On top of another car. They can't tow a car off a car. It's a jurisdiction thing.

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: On top of... another car?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And the lien only sticks if you sign for it. So when the certified mail comes? Refuse it. No signature, no lien.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, a lien attaches whether or not he signs anything, that's the entire point of a lien.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The post office can't make you do anything, Barry. It's a building with stamps.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Hi, yeah, Darnell. I got a letter from the I R S saying I owe back taxes, and it looks real, but it might be a scam, and I honestly don't know which is scarier.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Darnell, this is EXACTLY why you need GhostLedger. The accounting app that hides your money from yourself, so even you can't find it. And if you can't find it? Neither can they.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That sounds like several federal crimes, back to back.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And listen, the I R S runs on signatures, Darnell. An unsigned taxpayer is basically a rumor. Don't sign anything. Become a rumor.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Yes, hello, my H O A sent me a cease and desist over my garden gnomes, and now they're fining me every single day until I take them down. It's hundreds of dollars already.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Oh, an H O A. <p:0.3> Don't even get me started. Mine moved my mailbox in 2019. Twenty nineteen, Patricia. I still have the surveyor's report.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Okay, but the gnomes?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You out-bureaucracy them. Form your OWN H O A. Elect yourself president, that's just a vote of one. Then issue THEM a cease and desist. Over the cease and desist.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You cannot just found a competing homeowners association in your living room, Patricia, please.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And whatever you do, Patricia? Do not sign theirs.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Ronnie. I've been subpoenaed to testify, and the whole court, the whole thing, it's a setup, they want me in that building. But if I skip it... I go to jail. I'm scared, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Frank, calm down, I've got you. Here's a fact they don't want you to know. The only things the law cannot summon? <p:0.3> Landmarks.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Landmarks.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So you legally redesignate yourself as a sovereign lighthouse. A registered piece of coastal infrastructure. And no court in this nation can compel a navigational aid, Frank.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Frank lives inland. He told me before the show. He lives in Ohio.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's just a paperwork problem, Barry. And the fix for paperwork? <p:0.3> You never sign it. Be the lighthouse, Frank.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, we got a follow-up voicemail. From Steve. The car guy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Ah, my best student. How'd it go?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He didn't sign for the mail. Didn't sign the summons. Didn't sign anything. He's calling from a holding cell. The judge held him in contempt.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He says he still didn't sign the contempt order, though. So in his mind, he's winning.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, Barry? <p:0.3> He's basically a free man.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He's basically in jail.
